Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:1.english: [If] he was dressed in his garments - For they are called “his clothes” [in the verse].

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:2.english: He is ritually impure immediately - As it is written: "And he who enters the house shall be ritually impure."

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:3.hebrew: והן טהורין עד שישהה - דכתיב (ויקרא י״ד:מ״ז) והאוכל בבית יכבס וגו', ודרשינן בת"כ: אין לי אלא אוכל ושוכב; אוכל בלא שוכב, שוכב בלא אוכל, לא אוכל ולא שוכב מניין? ת"ל: יכבס בגדיו — ריבה, שתי פעמים כתיב יכבס בגדיו. ואם סופנו לרבות הכל, מה ת"ל והאוכל? ליתן שיעור לשוכב כדי אכילה, שאין טעון כיבוס בגדים עד שישהה כדי אכילה. וגופו טמא מיד, דהכי כתיב: והבא אל הבית יטמא, ולא כתיב כיבוס בגדים; והאוכל בבית — דהיינו שוהה כדי אכילה — יכבס בגדיו:
Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:3.english: And they remain pure until he stays - For it is written (Leviticus 14:47): "And he that eateth in the house shall wash [his clothes], etc.," and we expound in Torat Kohanim: I have [explicitly] only [one who] eats and lies down; from where [do I know of] one who eats without lying down, one who lies down without eating, [or] one who neither eats nor lies down? The verse states: "shall wash his clothes" — it amplified; twice it is written: "shall wash his clothes." And if in the end we include everything, why does the verse state: "And he that eateth"? To give a measure to the one who lies down [equal to] the duration of eating, that he does not require washing of clothes until he stays long enough to eat. And his body becomes impure immediately, for so it is written: "And he that goeth into the house... shall be unclean" (Leviticus 14:46), and washing of clothes is not written [there]; and "he that eateth in the house" — that is, one who stays long enough to eat — "shall wash his clothes."

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:4.hebrew: אכילת פרס - חצי ככר שיערו חכמים אותו למזון שתי סעודות לעירוב, דתנן בעירובין (דף פב:): חציה לבית המנוגע:
Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:4.english: The eating of a peras - [A peras is] half of the loaf that the Sages evaluated as food for two meals for an eiruv, as we learned in a mishna in Eruvin (82b): "Half of it for a leprous house."

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:5.english: Wheat bread - For it was smaller than that of barley.

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:6.hebrew: מיסב - דהיינו דרך אכילה — מי שהוא מיסב, הוא עסוק באכילה ואינו טרוד בדברים אחרים:
Rashi on Sukkah 6a:1:6.english: Reclining - That is, the [standard] manner of eating — one who is reclining is occupied with eating and is not preoccupied with other things.

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:2:1.english: A bone the size of a barley grain - From a corpse.

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:2:2.hebrew: ואינו מטמא באהל - כשיעור זה, עד שיהא שדרה או גלגולת שלמה, או רוב מנין אברי אדם:
Rashi on Sukkah 6a:2:2.english: And it does not impart impurity in a tent - [Only] at this measure, until there is a spine or a complete skull, or the majority of the number of a person's limbs.
